newsitem.title: USA: Kodak net jumps 21 percent, stock rises.
newsitem.headline: Kodak net jumps 21 percent, stock rises.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co. Tuesday said its earnings jumped 21 percent in third quarter, exceeding expectations on Wall Street, and cited strong sales of film and other products in North America, Russia and China.

The world's largest maker of film and photographic paper said net income jumped to $410 million, or $1.22 a share, from $338 million, or 99 cents a share, in the 1995 quarter. Revenues grew 8 percent to $4.18 billion from $3.88 billion.

Analysts had forecast profits of $1.20 a share on average, according to First Call, which tracks earnings estimates, and Kodak's stock added $1.50 to $79.375 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Rochester, N.Y.-based Kodak said sales to consumers rose 13 percent in the quarter, while commercial sales grew 5 percent.
But operating earnings grew faster on the commercial side of the business, up 42 percent, led by motion picture films, copiers and other imaging products.

Operating earnings in its consumer business edged up 3 percent, constrained by higher advertising and promotional spending, partly for the summer Olympics, and lower earnings in photofinishing operations outside the United States, Kodak said.

"While the third quarter sales growth in Consumer Imaging was very strong, we intend to focus on bringing profit growth more in line with sales growth," Chief Executive Officer George Fisher said in a statement.

For the nine months, net earnings grew 15 percent to $1.12 billion, or $3.32 a share, from $977 million, or $2.86 a share, from the 1995 period. Sales rose 7 percent to $11.65 billion from $10.89 billion.
Kodak's stock gained $1 to $78.875 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
